match_hough_3d — 3D match_localize op

• Data kinds: voxel × voxel → position

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.match_hough_3d(scene, template, device='cpu', ndir=26, mc=0.05, topk=1, nms=3, subvoxel=True) (to call the implementation directly, import match3d; match3d.match_hough_3d(scene, template, device='cpu', ndir=26, mc=0.05, topk=1, nms=3, subvoxel=True); from the registry, ops3d.get("match_hough_3d"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.match_hough_3d(...) returns only the declared out type position (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.match_hough_3d.raw(...) or call match3d.match_hough_3d directly.

• GPU: this op has a GPU path (device="cuda")

Usage

Generalized Hough 3-D (Ballard R-table voting). The voxel × Hough column.

Formulates GHT natively for the GPU as the sum of correlations per orientation bin:

accumulator A(t) = Σ_bin ( scene_bin ⋆ template_bin ). Each edge votes according to its gradient direction, and missing edges only lower the peak (robust to occlusion and clutter). Unlike shape-based (a single solution of continuous dot products), its distinguishing feature is that it returns the vote accumulator, so NMS yields multiple peaks = multiple instances. Returns [votes, d, h, w] of shape (topk,4) (votes descending).

Procedure: the unit gradients of both volumes (mc is a threshold on the raw output of sobel3d) are quantised to the nearest of ndir reference directions, and for each direction bin "the scene's 2-valued field for that bin ⋆ the template's 2-valued field for that bin" is summed via conv3d. It is divided by the number of valid template edges, so votes are in [0, 1]; 1 means all edges match.

• ndir: 26 or fewer takes the first ndir entries of the list of 26-neighbourhood directions (below 26 the directions are biased); 27 or more is

uniform on a fibonacci sphere. Coarser directions are more tolerant of rotation but also produce more false peaks.

• Each row of the return value (topk, 4) is [votes, z, y, x], votes descending. The coordinates are the scene coordinates of the template centre (T//2);

with subvoxel=True, the centroid of the ±2 neighbourhood.

• nms: each time a peak is taken, a cube of ±nms voxels is squashed to −1 before searching for the next. For nearby

multiple instances, make nms small.

• If the template has no edges, an all-0 (topk,4). Positions where the template does not fit entirely are 0.

Downstream: refine each peak with refine_translation_lk / refine_peak_newton.
